objects.description: Opaque pointer to memory-mapped file data returned by mmapFile. It represents a contiguous memory region mapped from a file. The header does not define a custom type; this is the built-in void pointer used as a handle to the mapped data.

Pointer to a size_t used as an out-parameter by mmapFile to receive the size of the mapped region. Not a custom typedef; included here only if treating built-in pointer as the out-parameter handle. The header defines no custom data types.

functions.name: mmapFile
functions.signature: void* mmapFile(const char* path, size_t* outSize);
functions.description: Maps the contents of a file into memory and returns a pointer to the mapped region; writes the size of the mapped region to outSize. Intended for efficient, file-backed access without copying. Exact access permissions, error signaling, and mapping lifetime semantics are not documented here and remain unknown.
requirements: path must be a valid, non-null C string naming a file (inferred from the function name and typical mmap patterns).
outSize should be a non-null pointer where the function will store the size of the mapped region (inferred).
The caller should not modify the file or unmap concurrently in ways that invalidate the mapping (unknown/unspecified; typical constraint).
On success, the caller is responsible for releasing the mapping by calling unmapFile with the returned pointer and the size written to outSize (inferred).
The returned pointer should be treated as a memory-mapped region; accessing it after it has been unmapped is invalid (inferred).
Error return convention (e.g., returning NULL on failure) is unknown; callers must be prepared for unspecified failure signaling.

functions.name: unmapFile
functions.description: Releases a previously created file mapping. The data argument is the pointer returned by mmapFile, and size is the exact mapping size associated with that pointer. After this call, the mapping is invalid and must not be accessed.
requirements: data must be the non-null pointer previously returned by mmapFile (inferred).
size must exactly match the size value originally returned via outSize from the corresponding mmapFile call (inferred).
Each mapping must be unmapped exactly once; do not call unmapFile multiple times on the same pointer (inferred).
After unmapFile returns, the memory region referenced by data must not be accessed (inferred).
Behavior on invalid pointers, mismatched size, or double unmapping is unspecified.

data_types.description: A C-style string representing a valid filesystem path to an existing file. It may include directories, file name, and extension. Must be null-terminated and refer to a file accessible by the process.

Raw bytes stored in a file with no assumed encoding or structure. The function reads or memory-maps the entire file content as-is; contents can be any sequence of bytes, including zeros or non-text data.
